subject: FinApps: Confirming deletion/RTBF requirements & backup constraints
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Foster <samuel.foster@finapps.com>, security@finapps.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-17T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: FinApps: Confirming deletion/RTBF requirements & backup constraints

Hi Sam / FinApps security team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear prioritization on user-level deletion and auditability. Short recap of what we captured, plus clarifying questions and proposed next steps.

Scope we heard on the call:
- PII types in scope: user identifiers (email, customer_id), payment method tokens (not full PANs), customer-provided documents (id scans), and derived embeddings tied to user ids.
- Data stores: primary application DB (Postgres, us-east-1), embeddings store (S3 + vector index), model KV cache (ephemeral on GPUs), analytics event logs (ELK).
- Residency: primary storage in us-east; FinApps requires no cross-border copies outside US.

Key constraints you mentioned:
- Deletion from primary stores: target 45 days from request.
- Need evidence: deletion audit logs and a signed attestation for compliance.
- Backups: mandate removal or acceptable mitigations for long-term snapshots.

Questions we need from you to finalize a MAP:
1) Confirm canonical list of PII fields (CSV or doc) we should search for.
2) Are there any legal holds or exceptions for specific accounts?
3) Acceptance threshold: is key-destruction for cold backups acceptable, or must bits be overwritten?

Proposed immediate next steps (tentative):
- FinApps: send canonical PII field list and note any legal holds (2 business days).
- Redwood: produce a draft deletion workflow (3 business days) and a canary deletion plan for a single test account.
- Joint: run canary deletion, review artifacts, then schedule full purge.

I attached the deletion schedule worksheet (deletion-schedule.xlsx) with our standard timelines and a column for alternate timelines if you need 45 vs 30 days. Also attached the SOC2 evidence request you asked for.

If this aligns, we can convert to a short MAP and route to Legal for signature.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: deletion-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet), FinApps-SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (pdf)

From: Samuel Foster <samuel.foster@finapps.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finapps.com, LegalOps <legal@finapps.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinApps: Confirming deletion/RTBF requirements & backup constraints

Rachel — thanks for the recap and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with Security/Legal: 

- Deletion windows: primary store deletion must complete within 45 calendar days of request.
- Backups: FinApps prefers bit-level purge where possible. For cold/immutable snapshots, FinApps can accept cryptographic key destruction of the backup if we receive an attestation plus proof that the backup is inaccessible. Key destruction must be scheduled and completed within 60 days where possible; we understand that some vendors may require longer and want to capture those explicitly.
- Auditability: we need immutable deletion audit logs (timestamped event ID, actor, object IDs removed) and a short signed attestation from Redwood ops for each batch purge.
- Embeddings: any embeddings that are uniquely tied to a user id must be purged. If embeddings are used to fine-tune shared models, additional controls are required.

One more ask: can you confirm whether your model-serving KV caches will retain any user-derived tokens after a session? We need assurance that session caches do not persist user PII beyond ephemeral TTL.

I attached a short evidence request template (FinApps-SOC2-evidence-request.pdf) with items we will need during our compliance review.

Sam
Head of Security, FinApps
samuel.foster@finapps.com

Subject: Re: FinApps: Confirming deletion/RTBF requirements & backup constraints

Sam — thanks, noted. Below is a concrete proposed deletion workflow based on your constraints; please flag anything that is unacceptable and we will update.

Proposed Redwood deletion workflow (draft):
1) Scope confirmation (0-3 business days): FinApps provides canonical PII map and legal hold list.
2) Inventory & mapping (3-7 business days): Redwood runs a scoped scan across application DB, embeddings index, analytics logs, and object storage; produces a list of object IDs to delete.
3) Canary deletion (7-14 days): Redwood performs a canary purge for a single sandboxed account; provides deletion audit log and attestation for the canary.
4) Full purge (target 30 calendar days post-approval; we can extend to 45 if you require): Redwood executes deletion from primary stores and returns a deletion manifest with event IDs and timestamps.
5) Backup/archives (60-180 days window): We recommend the following hierarchy:
   - Hot snapshot streams: purge within 60 days where vendor support exists.
   - Offsite cold snapshots: where immediate bit-level purge is not possible, Redwood proposes cryptographic key destruction and attestation as an acceptable mitigation; we will include vendor-specific timelines in the MAP.
6) Audit & attestation: Redwood will provide immutable deletion logs, a signed attestation, and a short runbook entry describing the steps taken.

Notes on caches/serving:
- Model KV caches are ephemeral by design and do not persist beyond the GPU session. We will enforce TTL <= 24hrs for session-level caches and record cache evictions in the deletion manifest.

Attachments: I uploaded a draft deletion-schedule.xlsx with alternative timelines columns (30/45/60 day options) and a sample deletion manifest template.

If you confirm the PII map and legal holds, we will convert this into a MAP and route to Legal. Also happy to run the canary the week of Jan 25 if that works on your side.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-19T10:00:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: engineering constraints and backup mitigation options

Quick internal note — copying here for the record before we finalize the MAP:

- Snapshot providers: some of our managed snapshot vendors have immutable retention policies that make bit-level deletion across older snapshots infeasible without vendor cooperation. We should capture vendor timelines explicitly in the MAP and flag any multi-month windows.
- Key destruction option: engineering is comfortable providing cryptographic key destruction for encrypted cold backups as an auditable mitigation. We should add a short technical appendix describing how key destruction renders backups unrecoverable, plus a vendor attestation step.
- Legal hold flow: if LegalOps requests a hold, we need an immediate stop to deletion and a separate escalation path; include estimated time-to-frozen-state (24-48 hours).

Also, we should confirm any cost delta for accelerated backup purges. I'll ask infra for an estimate and add it to the SOW.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samuel Foster <samuel.foster@finapps.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finapps.com, LegalOps <legal@finapps.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinApps: Confirming deletion/RTBF requirements & backup constraints

Thanks Rachel and Ben — this plan is clear and mostly acceptable. A few confirmations before Legal signs off: 

- FinApps will accept cryptographic key destruction for cold archives where immediate bit purge is not technically achievable, provided Redwood supplies:
  * A signed attestation outlining the key destruction process,
  * Deletion manifests and immutable logs for primary stores, and
  * Vendor-specific timelines for any snapshots that will take longer than 60 days.

- We confirm the canary the week of Jan 25. Please propose a single sandbox account and an observable checklist for success criteria.

Next steps on our side: Legal will issue a short MAP/SOW template and route for signature once we have your final deletion schedule filled (the sheet you sent) and the PII map.

If you can route the MAP to legal@finapps.com and copy me, we will prioritize review. Appreciate the responsiveness.

Sam
Head of Security, FinApps
